notes: §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR3 makes WRITE ... FROM "equivalent to the execution of the following statements in the order specified": "MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1" under the MOVE statement's rules, then "The same WRITE statement without the FROM phrase." KeyedIoBinder.BindWrite binds the phrase through MoveBinder.BindFromPhrase, which hands identifier-1 and record-name-1 to BindMoveOf, the one application of the MOVE rules; KeyedIoEmitter.EmitWrite emits that bound move first and then the code path a WRITE without FROM takes. No edition arm in the move; the one 1985 difference is the gate VersionConformancePass.VisitRecordFromPhrase, which refuses FROM literal-1 at --std 85 (COBOL0871), since the 1985 format prints only identifier-1. The witness writes from a shorter alphanumeric item over a record filled with Z and reads the space-padded record back. Probed further at --std 85: a numeric sender to a numeric record aligns on the decimal point, a longer sender truncates, a JUSTIFIED RIGHT record right-justifies, a group sender with a COMP item moves byte for byte, and each record reads back as moved; the move is done when the WRITE then fails with status 22; an alphanumeric-edited sender to a numeric record draws COBOL0819 and an index data item COBOL0809. A sender in the record's own storage draws nothing; that is the syntax rule §1985:IX.4.9.3 SR1, kb/Work PB5077, not this rule.

next.reason: 2023 adds FROM literal-1 (§2023:14.9.51.4 GR5: "MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1"), which the 1985 format refuses; the FROM identifier-1 case is unchanged. 1985 GR3: WRITE ... FROM = 'MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1' per MOVE rules, then the WRITE without FROM. §2023:14.9.51.4 GR5 keeps it ('The same WRITE statement without the FROM phrase'); §2023:14.9.51.3 SR6 restates that the implicit MOVE follows MOVE's rules. FROM literal-1 is refused by 1985's format, and GR5's overlap/undefined note reaches only storage 1985 SR1 forbids or 1985 MOVE already left undefined; neither is refused by this rule. Same.
